THIRD-PARTY NOTICES — Social Media Posts API dashboard image
================================================================

This project's own source is licensed under the Apache License 2.0
(see /app/LICENSE if copied, or the Git repository LICENSE file).
Apache-2.0 does not replace third-party terms for libraries shipped
inside the dashboard container image.

PROMINENT NOTICE — LGPL-3.0-or-later library
---------------------------------------------
The dashboard image includes a dynamically linked copy of libvips
(and related native libraries) supplied by the npm package:

  @img/sharp-libvips-linuxmusl-x64@1.3.4
  SPDX: LGPL-3.0-or-later
  libvips version recorded by that package: 8.18.7
  (see third-party/sharp-libvips-linuxmusl-x64-1.3.4.versions.json)

sharp@0.35.5 itself is Apache-2.0. It loads libvips at runtime from
the shared library shipped beside it (typically libvips-cpp.so.8.18.7).

License texts accompanying this image:
  third-party/licenses/LGPL-3.0.txt
  third-party/licenses/GPL-3.0.txt
(LGPL-3.0 incorporates GPL-3.0 by reference; both are included.)

CORRESPONDING SOURCE (version-matched)
---------------------------------------
libvips 8.18.7 source archive (upstream tag, verified reachable):
  https://github.com/libvips/libvips/archive/refs/tags/v8.18.7.tar.gz

Prebuilt binary package actually linked by this image (npm tarball):
  https://registry.npmjs.org/@img/sharp-libvips-linuxmusl-x64/-/sharp-libvips-linuxmusl-x64-1.3.4.tgz

The versions.json file lists additional native libraries bundled with
that prebuilt (glib, png, webp, and others) and their upstream versions.
Those components keep their own licenses. This notice is not a claim
that every bundled library is LGPL, and it is not a relicensing of
this project's source.

REPLACING THE LGPL LIBRARY
---------------------------
libvips is used as a shared library, not statically linked into the
project's JavaScript. A recipient may replace the shipped .so files
under:

  /app/node_modules/@img/sharp-libvips-linuxmusl-x64/lib

with an interface-compatible build (same SONAME / libvips-cpp.so.8
series) and rebuild or derive a new image. Example:

  docker build -f apps/dashboard/Dockerfile -t my-dashboard .
  # or, from a running derived image, replace the lib directory and
  # restart the container as user nextjs.

Source is conveyed only by the durable public URLs above for the exact
versions named here.

BASE IMAGES
-----------
This image is built FROM node:22-alpine. Node.js and Alpine Linux
licenses apply to those layers and are not replaced by Apache-2.0.
The Compose stack also runs upstream image caddy:2 (not republished
by this project).
